questions.question: Write a design brief and three specification points for a product that helps elderly people open jar lids.

points.text: Brief: 'Design and make a device that enables elderly users with reduced grip strength to open vacuum-sealed jar lids safely and independently.' Specification: 1) Must accommodate jar diameters from 50-100 mm. 2) Must require no more than 20 N of grip force. 3) Must be manufacturable for under 8 GBP retail cost.

questions.question: Explain the difference between a design brief and a design specification.

points.text: Design brief: a short statement describing the PROBLEM to solve - who, what, context. Does NOT specify the solution. Design specification: a detailed, measurable list of CRITERIA the final product must meet. The brief asks 'what is the problem?'; the specification answers 'what must the solution achieve?'

questions.question: A designer wants to create a new type of school bag. Describe three research methods they should use and explain what each would reveal.

points.text: 1) User interviews with students - reveal what they carry, pain points, preferences. 2) Observation of students using bags - reveals actual behaviour vs what they say. 3) Competitor analysis - identifies feature gaps, price points, common failure points.

questions.question: Full-Mark Response A company has identified that cyclists struggle to carry groceries on their bicycles. Write a design brief, produce a specification with at least six measurable points, and describe two research methods. <div class="

points.text: A grade 9 response will: Brief: 'Design and make a device that enables urban cyclists to safely carry up to 10 kg of groceries on a standard commuter bicycle without affecting stability.' Specification: 1) Carry up to 10 kg. 2) Fit bicycles with 20-28 inch wheels without tools. 3) Maintain stability at 15 mph. 4) Weather-resistant (IPX4). 5) Retail cost under 40 GBP. 6) Device weight under 1.5 kg when empty. Research: 1) Observation at supermarkets. 2) Interviews with cyclists about grocery volumes and pain points.
